answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. A registry records the lock and limits each account’s influence to its bonded amount, so creating a thousand aliases does not multiply voting power unless the attacker also multiplies capital. If a challenge proves coordinated fraud, a defined portion is forfeited. The echo of one operator across a nebula of accounts is therefore costly to sustain; the stake acts as a harbor for accountability, not proof that identities are unique.
